# Testament of Issachar — 5
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

1:1 A copy of the words of Issachar. For he called his sons and said to them:
1:2 Hearken, my children, to Issachar your father; give heed to the words of him who is beloved of the LORD.
1:3 I was born the fifth to Jacob as a reward for the mandrakes.
1:4 For Reuben my brother brought mandrakes from the field, and Rachel met him and took them.
1:5 And Reuben wept, and Leah my mother came forth to him.
1:6 And Rachel said to her: Let Jacob be thine this night for thy son's mandrakes.
1:7 And Jacob knew Leah that night, and she conceived and bore me; and on account of the reward she called my name Issachar.

2:1 Then came an angel of the LORD to Leah, and said: Two children more shalt thou bear, since thou hast given to thy sister the mandrakes because of thy modesty, and the LORD was pleased.
2:2 And the angel appeared also to Rachel, that she should not be fruitless for ever; for she would conceive, and it would be later than all the children of Leah.
2:3 And she gave up the mandrakes for the sake of children, according to the word of the angel of the LORD.

3:1 For I was a simple man and I tilled the ground, and I brought forth fruits of the field for my father Jacob; and my father loved me, for my simplicity.
3:2 And with the fruit of my labour I enriched my father and gave also to the poor of the land.
3:3 I ate of the good things of the earth only, and I had no wickedness in me.
3:4 I knew not of any sin in myself; my days were consumed in simplicity.
3:5 And I had no double mind toward any man, and no hatred in my heart toward anyone; I was always in singleness of heart.

4:1 I loved the LORD with all my strength; likewise also I loved every man as I love my children.
4:2 Do ye also these things, my children, and every spirit of Beliar will flee from you, and no deed of wicked men will have dominion over you.
4:3 Guard therefore simplicity, my children, and walk in singleness of heart, not prying into the affairs of your neighbor; but love the LORD and love your neighbor; pity the poor and the weak.
4:4 Bow your back in husbandry, and labour in all manner of works of the earth, offering gifts to the LORD in thankfulness.
4:5 For with the first-fruits of the earth will the LORD bless you, even as he blessed all the saints from Abel even unto this day.
4:6 For no other inheritance was given to you save that of the fruit of the earth.

5:1 Know ye therefore, my children, that in the last times your sons will forsake simplicity, and will cleave to insatiable desire; and leaving guilelessness behind will draw near to malice; and forsaking the commandments of the LORD, they will cleave to Beliar.
5:2 And they will leave husbandry, and will follow after their own wicked devices, and will be dispersed among the nations, and will serve their enemies.
5:3 Tell ye therefore these things to your children, that, if they sin, they may the more quickly return to the LORD.
5:4 For he is merciful, and will deliver them, and will bring them back into their land.

6:1 And behold I am a hundred and twenty-six years old and I perceive in me no sin.
6:2 Except my wife I have not known any woman; I have not committed fornication by the uplifting of my eyes.
6:3 I drank not wine, to be led astray thereby; I coveted not any desirable thing that was my neighbor's.
6:4 Guile arose not in my heart; a lie passed not through my lips.
6:5 If any man were in distress I joined my sighs with his, and I shared my bread with the poor.
6:6 I wrought godliness all my days and truth.
6:7 I loved the LORD; likewise also every man with all my heart.
6:8 Do ye also these things, my children, and every spirit of Beliar shall flee from you.

7:1 And when he had said these things, he commanded his sons that they should carry him up to Hebron and bury him there with his fathers.
7:2 And he stretched out his feet and fell asleep in peace.

---
*End of Testament of Issachar*
